newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks lose their nerve and slip lower.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks lose their nerve and slip lower.

text.p: Madrid stocks lost their nerve along with other European stock markets and slipped lower on Thursday, shaken by interest rate comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
The General index ended down 6.72 points, 1.42 percent, at 467.54, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares slipped 76.60 points, 1.41 percent, to 5,355.46.
"Greenspan's comments have broken support on the Ibex index at 5,400, but the market is not overly nervous and if we see other markets recovering, funds will return," one trader said.
Traders said Greenspan's comments had fuelled fears of a preemptive rise in interest rates at next Tuesday's Fed policy meeting.
Telefonica accounted for almost 17 percent of turnover and lost 35 pesetas, 1.03 percent, to 3,365, after announcing it was in talks with U.S. telecoms firms.
Among other individual stocks, Adolfo Dominguez ended 240 pesetas down at 4,820 on its third day of trading.
Repsol lost 60 pesetas to 5,790 and Endesa slipped 120 pesetas to 9,110.
Among banks, BBV and Popular dropped by more than two percent.
